rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is nonexistent, so this experiment tests the baseline performance of an RNA-only model with PCA encoding. It clarifies the potential of RNA data alone as a starting point, which is critical for comparison with multimodal approaches. This is the best use of the first experiment to establish a reference baseline.

The existing evidence shows that RNA-only singleprofile with PCA and no aggregation achieves 0.48 accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile with avgpool aggregation, which could reveal if multi-profile data and aggregation methods improve performance. It clarifies the impact of profile setting and aggregation, critical factors with weak prior evidence, while keeping RNA encoder and image settings consistent.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile RNA-only models (config_002, 0.590664 accuracy) outperform singleprofile RNA-only models. This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool (used in config_002) with transformer aggregation improves performance in multiprofile RNA-only setups. It isolates the effect of aggregation method, a critical design choice, while maintaining consistency with the current best configuration. This balances exploitation of the multiprofile RNA-only direction with exploration of alternative aggregation strategies.

The existing evidence shows that multiprofile RNA-only models with avgpool aggregation (config_002, 0.59 accuracy) outperform singleprofile and transformer aggregation. This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (a more advanced representation) while maintaining the effective multiprofile/avgpool setup could further improve accuracy. This isolates the impact of RNA encoder quality, a key design choice, and builds on the promising multiprofile direction.

Existing evidence shows that RNA-only models with scvi_n200 encoder and multiprofile setting (config_005) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.650). This experiment tests adding image data (resnet50) to this strong baseline, using avgpool aggregation (proven effective in RNA-only) and concat fusion. It isolates the impact of multimodal inputs while building on a validated RNA encoder and aggregation method, balancing exploitation of current strengths with exploration of image data's potential.

The existing evidence shows that RNA-only models with scvi_n200 encoder (config_005: 0.650 accuracy) outperform multimodal baselines. However, multimodal approaches with better image encoders (e.g., imagenet_vit_l) may offer gains. This experiment tests combining scvi_n200 RNA with imagenet_vit_l image encoder (a stronger image encoder than resnet50) using avgpool and concat fusion, which directly addresses the uncertainty about whether superior image encoders can surpass RNA-only performance. It isolates the effect of image encoder quality while leveraging the best RNA encoder, balancing exploration and exploitation.

The existing evidence shows that config_036 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200+imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.715). This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from 'concat' to 'weighted' in the same configuration improves accuracy. It isolates the effect of fusion strategy, a critical design choice, while keeping other components (model, profile, encoder, aggregation) consistent. This comparison could reveal if weighted fusion better leverages multimodal interactions, directly advancing toward the optimal configuration within remaining budget.

Existing evidence shows that config_036 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.715). This experiment tests replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation while keeping other components the same, to determine if more complex aggregation improves performance. It directly isolates the effect of aggregation method, a critical design choice, and builds on the success of the current top-performing configuration.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, transformer aggregation, and concat fusion (e.g., config_038) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests whether using resnet50 as the image encoder (instead of imagenet_vit_l) with the same aggregation/fusion strategy could maintain or improve performance, clarifying the impact of image encoder choice. It is the best use of the final experiment to validate if the current best configuration's success is robust to changes in image encoder.

The existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, and weighted fusion achieves high accuracy (0.720714 in config_038). This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool aggregation with transformer aggregation (a more complex method) further improves performance. It isolates the effect of aggregation strategy, a critical design choice, and leverages the strong foundation of the current top-performing configuration.
